newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee considers closing nuclear power plant.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee considers closing nuclear power plant.

text.p: Maine Yankee said on Tuesday that it is considering permanently closing its 910 megawatt (MW) Maine Yankee nuclear power plant and will slash spending on the unit until a decision on its future has been made.

The 25-year-old plant, in Wiscasset, Maine, has been shut since December 6, 1996, for extensive repairs and upgrades which must be carried out before the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) will allow it to return to service.

Maine Yankee chairman David Flanagan, speaking at a news conference here, said officials estimated that restarting the plant would cost $191 million and that the facility will not be restarted as soon as its owners had originally thought.
Maine Yankee had projected a late-August restart.
Flanagan said spending on the plant will be reduced by $41 million from June through December, primarily by dismissing some 900 contract workers who were working on repairs.
He said discussions would continue with Peco Energy Co, which has expressed an interest in buying the facility.
But he said a factor contributing to Tuesday's move was the knowledge that any sale would not go as quickly as the current owners would like.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co, and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
Maine Yankee has not operated at full power since early 1995. Subsequent safety and management concerns prompted the NRC to place the plant on its Watch List of facilities needing closer inspection.
The Maine Yankee board in late 1996 approved $38 million in extra spending to address the plant's problems, and in February brought in Entergy Corp to supervise management and restart efforts.
